newsitem.title: FRANCE: Labour envoy named at France Telecom.
newsitem.headline: Labour envoy named at France Telecom.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has named former labour minister Michel Delebarre to lead discussions on labour issues at the heart of possible privatisation candidate France Telecom.

The Finance Ministry said in a statement the company "must continue to assure the public service duties defined by the law...Within this framework, adaptations may prove necessary to benefit its European and international development and to preserve its leading place in an essential sector."

France's six-week-old leftist government is weighing whether to go ahead with the plans of the previous centre-right government to partially sell France Telecom. It has suggested this sale may go ahead if employees are consulted and agree.
The planned sale of a minority 30 to 35 percent public stake worth around 50 billion francs was suspended after the left's upset victory in a parliamentary election on June 1.
White-collar workers at France Telecom favour the sale, but the Communist-backed CGT union is firmly against any privatisations. The Communists are joint partners in Socialist Jospin's government.
The statement said Delebarre would report to the government by September 5 after talks with partners, including personnel and trade unions.
Delebarre has taken on some of the toughest posts since he first joined the cabinet as Labour Minister in 1984. He has served as urban affairs, social affairs and transport minister.
He has a modest opinion of himself.
"I can't patch things together. I don't have that genius. But I'm a good technician," he once said.
